sourceDescriptionRaw: Want to get something printed on our 3D printer? Participants can choose a design from Thingiverse, or provide their own design. Designs must be in an.stl file format and able to be emailed or provided on a USB drive. We estimate that 3D prints will be ready for pickup within 7 days of submission. Designs are considered printable if able to load and save on a Creality K1C, but library staff have the right to refuse any print job. Color will depend on filament availability. All prints must take less than 1 hr 30 min (estimated 60 grams of filament). All prints are free and must meet the criteria above and below. Registration is required. Only 1 print per person and only 1 print per family/household per month. Please also be aware that: Prints are meant to be for personal use only and not for commercial purposes.No weapons or items that could be construed as a weapon will be accepted for print.Prints that are considered obscene or otherwise inappropriate for the library environment will be not accepted for print.The library’s 3D printers must be used only for lawful purposes. All local, state, and federal laws must be followed.Accepted prints may not violate any third party’s intellectual property, such as copyright, patent, or trademark.Library staff reserve the right to refuse any 3D print request.SJPL and library staff are not responsible for malfunctions or misprints. title: Parallel Career Path as a Professional Dancer
description: Join us for Guidance and Insight on Possible Parallel Career Paths, an engaging conversation featuring renowned choreographer Nirmala Madhava of PAMPA Dance Academy and Bay Area professional Sowmya.
parentSummary: Join us for Guidance and Insight on Possible Parallel Career Paths, an engaging conversation featuring renowned choreographer Nirmala Madhava of PAMPA Dance Academy and Bay Area professional Sowmya.
sourceDescriptionRaw: Join us for Guidance and Insight on Possible Parallel Career Paths, an engaging conversation featuring renowned choreographer Nirmala Madhava of PAMPA Dance Academy and Bay Area professional Sowmya. Nirmala brings decades of experience in Kathak and Bharatanatyam, global performances, university teaching, and cultural leadership at prestigious events. Her collaborations include working with acclaimed choreographer Lawrence Pech and contributing to the San Francisco Opera’s production of Aida. Sowmya, a Santa Clara University graduate, blends her business background with meaningful experience in college admissions and her current role on Levi Strauss & Co.’s Corporate Insights team. Together, they will share how passion, tradition, and professional skills can intersect to shape fulfilling parallel career paths. This session offers inspiration and practical guidance for anyone exploring multiple avenues in their personal or professional journey.Thank you to the Cupertino Library Foundation for making this event possible. title: Nightfall
description: Follow the story beyond the mansion onto a glowing woodland trail lined with 1,000 illuminated jack-o'-lanterns, towering scarecrows, giant glowing slugs, and artistic woodland installations before arriving at the enchanting Witches' Village hidden beneath the redwoods.
parentSummary: Follow the story beyond the mansion onto a glowing woodland trail lined with 1,000 illuminated jack-o'-lanterns, towering scarecrows, giant glowing slugs, and artistic woodland installations before arriving at the enchanting Witches' Village hidden beneath the redwoods.
sourceDescriptionRaw: By day, Filoli is a house frozen in elegance. By night, it's frozen in something else entirely. Wander into a Halloween harvest party in the Meadow, pumpkins, music, firelight, and slowly notice the mansion behind you isn't quite right. Something has taken root inside. Follow the trail of clues through a house reclaimed by nature, into a glowing woodland, and all the way to a witch's hidden village, where a century-old enchantment is finally coming undone. This is Nightfall: one story, told across an entire estate. Games, live music, food and drink, and thousands of pumpkins. The night starts light — before you notice the mansion watching. A witch has cast a curse on Filoli. Frozen in time, the House is reclaimed by the forest. Dinner party guests have disappeared, baffling the Lady of the House. Crows watch from above, dolls come alive, and the mansion's rooms are shrouded in mystery. The denizens of the forest are enchanted by the curse: hundreds of strolling scarecrows, glowing trees, giant slugs, and 1,000 glowing jack-o-lanterns follow you along the trail. Hidden beneath the redwoods a coven's gathering, a tarot reading that predicts your fate, magical brooms fly through the trees, and a giant cauldron looms over the Village. Eight minature trains endlessly loop in and out of the shadows, through 1,000 feet of track, and past a ghostly train conductor. Step into a new elegant lounge experience tucked inside Filoli’s grandest room, where flickering candlelight, gilded ceilings, and refined service set the stage for an unforgettable evening. Delight with a curated flight of exceptional champagnes as whispers of mystery drift through the historic House. Experience includes: Gather around for a hauntingly fun evening at our Nightfall Private Fire Pit Experience! Enjoy exclusive access to the Meadow, transformed into a magical autumnal escape just for you and your guests. Each experience promises not only warmth and ambiance, but also an intimate moment to connect with loved ones under the spellbinding night sky. Experience includes: As the sun sets and Nightfall comes alive, gather your guests for a private evening in Filoli's Garden House. Surrounded by festive lighting, seasonal ambiance, and the beauty of the estate after dark, this exclusive experience offers a sophisticated and memorable way to celebrate the season. Perfect for corporate gatherings, client appreciation events, milestone celebrations, holiday parties, and social occasions. Experience includes: Packages Start At: $10,000; includes 75 guests *Non-alcoholic option available Nightfall takes place across the Filoli Estate. There are step free route, with a mix of paved, gravel, mulch and field surfaces. We get spooky rain or shine. This is a family Friendly event, areas may be dimly illuminated or spooky in nature. Yes! Beyond our regular food offerings, the bars across the estate are brewing up a special menu with just the thing to warm you up as you undo the Witch's Spell. By day, Filoli is breathtaking. By night, the mystery begins. Start your evening at a lively harvest celebration filled with pumpkins, live music, seasonal food and drinks, festive games, and autumn charm. Then venture into the Historic House, where nature has slowly reclaimed every room and a century-old mystery waits to be uncovered. Follow the story beyond the mansion onto a glowing woodland trail lined with 1,000 illuminated jack-o'-lanterns, towering scarecrows, giant glowing slugs, and artistic woodland installations before arriving at the enchanting Witches' Village hidden beneath the redwoods. New this year, discover an incredible miniature railway with eight train loops, winding through the witches' enchanted world. Blending immersive storytelling, spectacular lighting, unforgettable photo moments, and seasonal fun, Nightfall is the Bay Area's ultimate fall and Halloween experience for families, couples, and friends.

title: The Songs of Nature: An Art Exhibit
description: Since then, we started watercolor painting together on Thursdays.
parentSummary: Since then, we started watercolor painting together on Thursdays.
sourceDescriptionRaw: Lisha and Helen's exhibit will be on display in the lobby during Saratoga Library's open hours from Monday August 31 to October 30, 2026. About the ExhibitLisha and Helen like to explore nature and often join the Los Gatos Art Association morning group to paint in oil. On Thursday mornings they join the Santa Clara Valley Watercolor Society to practice watercolor painting. They love nature and appreciate its beauty. Here are some glimpses of their observations of the natural beauty surrounding us. They hope you like their paintings. Helen Chen's Artist Statement My name is Helen Chen. Ever since I was a little girl, I liked to draw. I remembered after each class, I doodle on my books and notebooks. This habit lasted long into my school years and later in life. But at that time in China, there weren't any art classes I could take like the ones here in the United States. In addition, my parents didn't like the idea of me pursuing art. They were more concerned about me finding a good job for security and a good life. To them, this meant that I should become an engineer in the field of mathematics, physics or chemistry. They believed “学好数理化,走遍天下都不怕” or “Master math, physics, or chemistry, and you can go anywhere in the world without fear.”I took their practical advice and became an engineer. After working for a couple years in China, I came to America to pursue higher education. After I graduated and worked here for a few years, I discovered that the University Art store in San Jose offered oil painting classes. I joined the weekend oil painting workshop. However, because I didn't have any previous training, I found it extremely challenging and practiced intermittently. In 2012, I decided to take a watercolor and oil painting class at West Valley College. While I studied there, I met a lot of wonderful people and we became good friends. One of them introduced me to the Santa Clara Valley Watercolor Society (SCVWS). Since then, we started watercolor painting together on Thursdays. Through SCVWS I met a lot of kind and talented artists, and I am inspired by them. In addition, I go to the Los Gatos Art Association (LGAA) for oil painting. I also started learning from famous artists like Charles Reid, Ching Chung-Wei, and Richard Schmid by reading their books with a group of friends. Now, I mostly painted for fun and love to paint nature. I know I will have a long way to go to become a good artist, but I will keep going. Lisha's Artist StatementSince 2013, Lisha Wang has been an active member of plein air painting groups, the Santa Clara Watercolor Society and the Los Gatos art community. She loves to explore a variety of subjects and enjoys painting outdoors. Nature is her greatest inspiration, from blue skies, floating clouds, distant mountains and vast landscapes to small houses and barns in a field. She also loves painting people by capturing their emotions, posture and movements. These subjects have remained her favorite throughout the years.Lisha’s passion for painting began with the childhood activity of chalk drawing on concrete floors. She developed her painting skills by attending various art classes and live demonstrations of water color and oil painting, as while as participating in artist conferences. For more than 15 years, Lisha has enjoyed PleinAir painting with fellow artists. These experiences and practices have deepened her understanding of artistic expression as seen by human eyes. Lisha believes that painting is more than simply creating beautiful images. It is about observing the world with gratitude, and sharing moments of beauty with others by using brushes and colors.

sourceDescriptionRaw: Join us on Saturday, October 3rd from 10:30am-1pm, in the Campbell Library Community Room for a Children's Halloween Costume Swap! Bring a gently used costume with you to trade for a "new-to-you" option, or simply come and choose from our pre-donated selections! Don't know what a costume swap is? Here are some FAQs and our answers: Q. What is a costume swap?A. Great question! To swap means to trade, so bring a gently used costume to leave behind for another child to enjoy, and pick a "new" one for yourself.Q. If it's a swap, why do you have pre-donated costumes?A. We want to do our best to have choices for you! And also we want every kiddo to join even if they weren't able to bring a costume to trade this time.Q. Will you definitely have my size?A. We cannot guarantee that we will have your size, but hopefully you can find something that works or something to grow into.Q. Will there be scary costumes?A. Possibly. It will be up to you and your library adult to decide what the right costume is for you. Q. What will you do with the costume that I bring if no other child chooses it?A. We will donate it so that it makes its way to a great new owner!If you have other questions, feel free to ask us at the Children's Information Desk.For accessibility accommodations (ex. sourceDescriptionRaw: Join us for the FIRST FRIDAYS Art Walk and the final STREET MRKT indie urban art faire of the year! Bring friends and family for a unique night out in downtown. Stroll through all the exhibits hosted by downtown’s best galleries, and then enjoy STREET MRKT as it transforms S. 1st St. into an open air gallery full of incredible hyper-local artists & performers. Let’s come together to ensure that the arts, creativity and community thrive! Admission is free (spend it with the Artists!) and family friendly. SoFA District ANNO DOMINI // the second coming of Art & Design – 366 S. First St. map Opening reception in galleryTWO: Rider of Reverie Susiyo (Indonesia) solo exhibition In these new works, familiar everyday objects are inhabited with personality and energetic spirit. The real and the surreal move along a Möbius strip, with no distinction of where one begins and the other ends. Susiyo’s vivid imagination is brought to life through his highly skilled technical ability, utilizing composition and color to pull us into his sur/real worlds. Each painting offers a glimpse into a larger narrative, inviting us as viewers to imagine both the moments that came before and those still to come with unlimited possibilities. Ultimately, Susiyo reminds us that these imagined realms are not separate from our own and can help us expand how we see and shape our own world. Susiyo was born on February 12, 1993, in Semarang Regency, Indonesia. Susiyo’s artistic journey began with his early experiences in the animation industry, where he was involved in the production process of 2D animated films. This experience opened his eyes to the world of visual arts and became a gateway to further exploring his creative potential. Not stopping there, he continued his education at the Indonesian Institute of the Arts Yogyakarta, majoring in Fine Arts with a focus on Visual Communication Design. His university years became a crucial period in shaping his artistic identity. He not only learned artistic techniques formally but also broadened his horizons by actively participating in various art communities. His involvement in these communities provided Susiyo with opportunities to exchange ideas and hone his creativity, which eventually led him to the art exhibition stage. His participation in numerous group exhibitions marked a significant starting point in his professional journey as an artist, introducing his works to a wider audience and solidifying his presence in the art world. Rider of Reverie at Anno Domini is Susiyo’s debut solo exhibition. On view in galleryONE: A love letter to all the cars that could have hit me, but didn’t. Kazland (UK) solo exhibition A brand new collection of works that I began making during my recovery after being hit by a car last year. The accident itself wasn’t too bad but while I was healing it gave me the chance to work (very carefully) on lots of smaller pieces from my home, everything became more careful, and more meticulous. Using pencils and pastels more than paint became very important while I couldn’t move so much. Since then I’ve kept with the same way of working in a more considered fashion, and stepping back from what I’m doing to feel out the next moves. The collection focuses on the relationship between mortality and magic – and how we shouldn’t try to control the world around us. “Waiting for the swamp to float back to earth – feeding on whatever lands first. a cabin built from the leftovers, the collection above the fire is nearly complete. Decorated with only the rarest flowers and jewels from the riverbed we wait our turn. Through the gate – choose your own adventure – third times a charm. Burnt into the stone, I can see what you were trying to do. She’s made of shadows – you’ll never catch her – go live in the tree (starve on acorns) Trapped in the barn we made from spent matches. The door doesn’t open – It doesn’t have to.” About the Artist: Kazland, born Callum J. Buckland, 1990, is a self taught, mixed med…

title: CNPS: talk #2  Transforming HOA Landscapes with Native Plants & AB 1572
description: Attendees will leave with actionable steps for replacing thirsty turf with vibrant, ecosystem-friendly landscapes that satisfy state mandates while enhancing neighborhood character.Speaker Bio:Shelkie is a landscape designer and founder of WaterEfficientGardens.com, an online landscape design business specializing in low-water and California native garden designs.
parentSummary: Attendees will leave with actionable steps for replacing thirsty turf with vibrant, ecosystem-friendly landscapes that satisfy state mandates while enhancing neighborhood character.Speaker Bio:Shelkie is a landscape designer and founder of WaterEfficientGardens.com, an online landscape design business specializing in low-water and California native garden designs.
sourceDescriptionRaw: HOA Parking Strip landscaped with California Native Plants As California advances its water conservation goals, traditional HOA turf policies are undergoing a major shift. Starting January 1, 2029, Assembly Bill 1572 will prohibit the use of potable water for non-functional turf in HOA common areas - a mandate that will be strictly enforced. For homeowners and board members, this regulatory shift presents a powerful opportunity to replace lawn areas with native landscaping that conserves water and restores local biodiversity. In this presentation, Shelkie Tao will share why converting lawns to California native plants yields far greater long-term benefits than standard low-water alternatives. She will cover practical strategies for balancing ecological performance with polished visual appeal, selecting climate-appropriate species that thrive in structured garden settings, and effectively communicating design intent to HOA boards. Attendees will leave with actionable steps for replacing thirsty turf with vibrant, ecosystem-friendly landscapes that satisfy state mandates while enhancing neighborhood character.Speaker Bio:Shelkie is a landscape designer and founder of WaterEfficientGardens.com, an online landscape design business specializing in low-water and California native garden designs. As a sustainability-driven entrepreneur, she is committed to developing attractive, water-efficient, and ecosystem-friendly landscaping solutions. Her design work has been featured by the statewide Save Our Water campaign. Prior to founding Water Efficient Gardens, Shelkie worked for over a decade in the Silicon Valley high-tech industry. She earned a Certificate of Achievement in Environmental Horticulture and Design from Foothill College, holds an MBA from the UCLA Anderson School of Management, and is an avid trail runner who has completed 21 marathons.For accessibility accommodations (ex. title: Why Are Exoplanetary Systems Unlike the Solar System?
description: This sample of exoplanet systems enables us to study planetary systems as a population, and test planet formation theory.
parentSummary: This sample of exoplanet systems enables us to study planetary systems as a population, and test planet formation theory.
sourceDescriptionRaw: NASA's Kepler mission discovered over 4,400 transiting planets around other stars, including over 700 systems with multiple planets. This sample of exoplanet systems enables us to study planetary systems as a population, and test planet formation theory. The results are that our Solar System has a relatively rare configuration, and we don't know why. In this talk, we will explore the expectations of planet formation theory, and the constraints that are now available form observations, as we work toward the goal of understanding how common Earth-like worlds are and finding such cosmic neighbors.Speaker Daniel Jontof-Hutter is an associate professor of physics and astronomy at the University of the Pacific in Stockton. He studies planetary dynamics, what we can learn about planetary systems from their motion. His research goals include pushing the characterization of low-mass exoplanets toward the terrestrial regime, using big data and dynamical simulations. For accessibility accommodations (ex. title: Night Sky Journey
description: Finally, you’ll leave the Solar System and explore the stars and nebulae of our home galaxy, the Milky Way.
parentSummary: Finally, you’ll leave the Solar System and explore the stars and nebulae of our home galaxy, the Milky Way.
sourceDescriptionRaw: Join Docent Naturalists Liza Coe, Catherine Xun, Dave Kocsis, Naureen Moon, NASA scientists, and local amateur astronomers for an evening observing the night sky. Neptune and Saturn will be visible (weather permitting). You'll begin with a close-up look at rocks from the Moon, Mars, and across the Solar System. Gaze through telescopes for detailed views of the lunar surface, continue the journey farther to Saturn’s spectacular rings and moons, and then go beyond to blue Neptune. Finally, you’ll leave the Solar System and explore the stars and nebulae of our home galaxy, the Milky Way. (Note: This activity is not a hike but will be held in the Skyline Circle Parking Area, a short walk from where you’ll park your cars.) Bring layered clothing to stay warm. Reservations are required and will be accepted on or after October 3 at 12:00 p.m. (Noon) and close October 16 at 2:00 p.m.

title: Family Fun with Flowers
description: This is a morning of making something beautiful together, side by side at the same table.
parentSummary: This is a morning of making something beautiful together, side by side at the same table.
sourceDescriptionRaw: Bring the whole family for a hands-on flower arranging class, whether you’re an adult or a child. This is a morning of making something beautiful together, side by side at the same table. You’ll work in adult-and-child pairs, with all the containers, flowers, and materials provided. Our instructor will guide you step by step, so there’s nothing to prepare and no experience needed. By the end, each pair will have created two arrangements to take home, one to keep and one to give. Along the way you’ll pick up the simple techniques that make flowers look their best, the kind you can use again at your own kitchen table. Mostly, though, it’s about the pleasure of arranging flowers with someone you love, in the middle of the garden on a Saturday morning. No experience is needed. Just bring your curiosity, and gloves and clippers if you have them. Required Materials If you have them, please bring gloves, clippers (adult), and scissors (child). Instructor Bio Karen Flores earned her certificate in traditional floral design at Filoli. She spent over ten years there teaching family flower arranging classes. She currently teaches for local garden clubs, rose societies and the Pink Ribbon Good groups. Karen is an accredited Floral Design judge for the Garden Club of America and for the American Rose Society. She enjoys sharing her love of flowers with the younger generation. sourceDescriptionRaw: Give thanks to Native Californians by exploring how they cared for the land since time immemorial before the arrival of settler-colonialists. Join Docent Naturalists Marie Faust Evitt, Nancy Weintraub, and Megan Elmore for a moderately-paced hike along the beautiful Ipiwa, Alpine Loop, and Sunny Jim trails. You’ll observe grassland, chaparral, and riparian habitats while discovering how local Native tribes use strategies such as cultural burning and regular pruning to nurture plants and ensure abundant food and materials for homes, baskets, and medicine. Children who can comfortably hike more than four miles are welcome. Bring a snack for a break at Alpine Pond.

sourceDescriptionRaw: | Performances: December 2-3, 2026 | A holiday mash-up for the whole family, The Hip Hop Nutcracker returns for another spectacular tour. Directed and choreographed by Tony and Olivier Award-nominated Jennifer Weber, this contemporary dance spectacle is a re-mixed and re-imagined version of the classic, smashing hip hop dance and Tchaikovsky’s timeless music together into a heart-stirring and inspirational holiday event. The Hip Hop Nutcracker is brought to life by a powerhouse cast of a dozen all-star dancers, a DJ, a violinist, and MC Kurtis Blow, one of hip hop’s founding fathers, who opens the show with a short set. Just like the original, in The Hip Hop Nutcracker, Maria-Clara and the Nutcracker Prince go on a dream adventure battling a gang of mice, visiting the land of sweets and learning the lessons of the holiday season. Innovative digital graffiti and visuals transform the landscape of E.T.A. Hoffmann’s beloved story from traditional 19th Century Germany to the vibrant, diverse sights and sounds of contemporary New York City. Grab your family and friends and let the dynamic performers of The Hip Hop Nutcracker take you on a journey that celebrates love, community and the magic of the holiday season. title: Disney's Dare to Dream Jr.
description: As the trainees work together to discover their own dreams, they uncover the power that imagination and teamwork have to make anything possible.
parentSummary: As the trainees work together to discover their own dreams, they uncover the power that imagination and teamwork have to make anything possible.
sourceDescriptionRaw: | Performances: June 23-27 | Children's Musical Theater San Jose (CMT San Jose) presents Disney's Dare to Dream JR., a musical revue that follows an eager group of trainees on their first day at a fictional Walt Disney Imagineering Studio. As the trainees work together to discover their own dreams, they uncover the power that imagination and teamwork have to make anything possible. Celebrating 100 years of Disney music, the production features 20 songs spanning a century of beloved films, including selections making their stage debut alongside favorites from The Princess and the Frog, Coco, Encanto, and Frozen II. Now in its 59th season, CMT San Jose is one of the region's premier youth performing arts organizations, offering training and performance opportunities to thousands of young artists each year. CMT San Jose trains and educates today's youth through musical theater to set and achieve high artistic and personal goals, and to inspire them to become exemplary artists, patrons and citizens of tomorrow. The organization is dedicated to fostering creativity and a lifelong love of the performing arts in a supportive and inclusive environment. Performances: Wed., June 23, 2027 @ 7pm Thurs., June 24, 2027 @ 7pm Fri., June 25, 2027 @ 7pm Sat., June 26, 2027 @ 2pm, 7pm Sun., June 27, 2027 @ 11am, 3pm Tickets on sale as of May 28, 2027. > Montgomery Theater Events Calendar > Visitor FAQs __
